subject: physics
title: The electromagnetic spectrum
key_idea: Electromagnetic waves are transverse waves that transfer energy from a source to an absorber. They all travel at the same speed in a vacuum. They form a continuous spectrum, grouped by wavelength and frequency from radio waves to gamma rays.

blocks.text: This section covers what all electromagnetic waves have in common.

items.meaning: A transverse wave that transfers energy from a source to an absorber and can travel through a vacuum.
The number of waves passing a point each second, measured in hertz (Hz).
The distance from a point on one wave to the same point on the next wave, measured in metres (m).

items: All electromagnetic waves are **transverse** waves.
They transfer energy from a source to an absorber.
They need no medium, so they travel through a vacuum (space).
In a vacuum (and in air) they all travel at the same speed, about 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s.
Light is an electromagnetic wave, so it is part of the spectrum.

blocks.text: Different types of electromagnetic wave differ in frequency and wavelength, not in speed.

items: Electromagnetic waves are transverse and transfer energy from a source to an absorber.
They all travel at the same speed in a vacuum.
They differ in frequency and wavelength.

blocks.text: This section covers the seven groups in order and what our eyes can detect.
The groups form a continuous spectrum. There are no gaps between them.

items: Radio waves: longest wavelength, lowest frequency.
Microwaves.
Infrared.
Visible light, from red (longest wavelength) to violet (shortest).
Ultraviolet.
X-rays.
Gamma rays: shortest wavelength, highest frequency.

blocks.text: Going down the list, wavelength decreases and frequency increases.

items: Our eyes only detect visible light, which is a small part of the spectrum.
Infrared and ultraviolet were discovered late because we cannot see them.
New technology was needed to detect the waves beyond visible light.
The order is radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.
From radio to gamma, wavelength gets shorter and frequency gets higher.
Our eyes only detect visible light.

blocks.text: This section covers how to find the wavelength of an electromagnetic wave from its frequency.

blocks.label: Wave speed
where: wave speed is in metres per second (m/s). For electromagnetic waves in a vacuum it is 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s.

blocks.text: Because the speed is fixed, a higher frequency means a shorter wavelength.

items.text: For light of frequency 6.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz: wavelength = 3.0 × 10⁸ ÷ (6.0 × 10¹⁴)

diagram.alt: Change the frequency of an electromagnetic wave and see its wavelength. The speed stays the same.

outputs.label: Wave speed in a vacuum (does not change)

blocks.text: A frequency of 1 gives infrared, about 4 to 7.5 gives visible light and 10 gives ultraviolet.

diagram.alt: Calculate the wavelength of light in nanometres from its frequency.
diagram.question: Light has a frequency of {f} × 10¹⁴ Hz. The speed of light is 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. Calculate the wavelength of the light in nanometres (nm).
working: Multiply by 10⁹ to change metres to nanometres.

items: wave speed = frequency × wavelength applies to every electromagnetic wave.
Change units to Hz and m before you substitute.
In a vacuum the speed is the same, so higher frequency means shorter wavelength.

checks.q: State two things that are the same for all electromagnetic waves travelling in a vacuum.
checks.a: They are all transverse and they all travel at the same speed.

checks.q: Put these in order of increasing frequency: ultraviolet, radio waves, X-rays, infrared.
Microwaves have a frequency of 2.5 × 10⁹ Hz. The speed of electromagnetic waves is 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. Calculate the wavelength.

exam_phrases: they travel at the same speed (in a vacuum / air)
they can travel through a vacuum
different types of electromagnetic waves have a different frequency and a different wavelength
gamma has a higher frequency / a shorter wavelength

mistakes.wrong: Radio waves and gamma rays are similar because both can be reflected and refracted.
mistakes.right: Reflection and refraction are ignored for this question. Give the shared properties: same speed in a vacuum, can travel through a vacuum, transverse and electromagnetic.

mistakes.wrong: Different types of electromagnetic wave travel at different speeds.
mistakes.right: In a vacuum or air they all travel at the same speed. They differ in frequency and wavelength.

mistakes.wrong: Radio waves and gamma rays need a medium to travel through.
mistakes.right: They do not need a medium. They can travel through a vacuum.

worked_example.question:
Radio waves and gamma rays both transfer energy.

Give three other similarities between radio waves and gamma rays.
answer_points: They travel at the same speed in a vacuum (or air).
They can travel through a vacuum.
worked_example.tip: Any three of these score one mark each. 'They travel at the speed of light' and 'they do not need a medium' are accepted. Reflection, refraction, absorption and diffraction are ignored.

exam_phrases: radio waves and light waves travel at the same speed (in space)
X-rays always have a higher frequency than microwaves
all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed

mistakes.wrong: Radio waves take 40 minutes from Jupiter and light takes 8 minutes from the Sun, so radio waves are slower.
mistakes.right: Radio waves and light travel at the same speed in space. Jupiter is 40 ÷ 8 = 5 times further away.

mistakes.wrong: In a vacuum, X-rays and microwaves have the same frequency.
mistakes.right: They have the same speed. X-rays always have a higher frequency than microwaves.

mistakes.wrong: A fire mostly emits chemical waves and transfers infrared energy to the hands.
mistakes.right: The fire mostly emits infrared waves, and these transfer thermal energy to the hands.

worked_example.question:
This question is about the electromagnetic spectrum.

X-rays and microwaves are both parts of the electromagnetic spectrum.

Use words from the list to complete the sentences.

amplitude   frequency   longitudinal   speed   transverse   wavelength

X-rays and microwaves are both _____ waves.

In a vacuum, x-rays and microwaves always have the same _____.

X-rays always have a higher _____ than microwaves.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each word. The words must be in the correct order.

exam_phrases: both travel at the same speed / speed of light (in a vacuum)
X-ray has higher frequency / shorter wavelength
visible light has a larger frequency (than infrared)
we can only see a small part of the EM spectrum
new inventions / technology were needed to detect beyond visible light

mistakes.wrong: Visible light has a shorter frequency than infrared.
mistakes.right: Do not write longer or shorter frequency. Visible light has a larger (higher) frequency and a shorter wavelength than infrared.

mistakes.wrong: The difference between X-rays and visible light is that we can see visible light and cannot see X-rays.
mistakes.right: This is not allowed as a difference. Say X-rays have a higher frequency, a shorter wavelength or more energy.

mistakes.wrong: Infrared cannot be seen because it is not visible to the eye.
mistakes.right: This is ignored. Say our eyes can only detect a limited range of electromagnetic waves, and infrared is outside that range.

worked_example.question:
The speed of all electromagnetic radiation is 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

Ultra-violet waves typically have a frequency of 3000 THz.

Calculate the wavelength of these ultra-violet waves in nm.
worked_example.tip: The answer 100 nm scores all 3 marks. Writing the equation in symbols or words is not credited on its own.
